_provenance.notes: The Pacific Salmon Treaty (PST) was signed in 1985 and governs harvest of salmon that originate in one country but are caught in the waters of the other. Key panels: Northern Boundary (SE AK/BC), Transboundary Rivers (Stikine, Taku, Alsek), CBC (Columbia River Chinook), and Fraser River panels.

treaty_history.notes: First year of PST implementation. Signatories: USA and Canada.
PSC Annual Report 1990. Northern BC stocks declining.
PSC Annual Report 1994. Treaty near breakdown. Canada threatens termination.
PSC Annual Report 1999. New Annex IV implemented after 1999 renegotiation.
PSC Annual Report 2019. Treaty renegotiated to 2028.
PSC 2024 preliminary. Source: PSC Annual Report 2024 press release.
